questions.question: Ambubachi Mela (Fair) is held in which of the temples of North-East India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kamakhya.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ambubachi Mela (Fair):-**

 
 
• It is held in **Kamakhya temple**, which is located in **Guwahati, Assam.**
 
• The fair is celebrated during the **monsoon season**, usually in the month of **June or July, **and marks the **annual menstruation** of the goddess Kamakhya.
 
• During the fair, the temple remains** closed for three days**, and devotees are not allowed to worship the deity.
 
• After three days, the temple is **reopened**, and devotees **offer prayers and seek blessings.**
 
• The fair attracts a large number of devotees from all over India and abroad, and is considered one of the** most important festivals** in North-East India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dakshineswar Kali temple:-**

 
 
• It​ is located in** Kolkata, West Bengal,** and is famous for its association with **Sri Ramakrishna Paramahamsa.**
 
 
 
• **Bhuvaneswari temple:-**
 
 
• It is located in **Odisha, **and is dedicated to the goddess** Bhuvaneswari.**
 
 
 
• **Billeswar temple:-**
 
 
• It is located in **Assam,** and is dedicated to **Lord Shiva. **

• Gomat:-
 
 
• A wealthy person in the early Vedic period was known as **Gomat.**
 
• Gomat was a term used to describe a** rich and influential person** in the society.
 
• The term Gomat was derived from the Sanskrit word** 'gomati' **which means **possessing or having cows.**
 
• Cows were considered a** symbol of wealth and prosperity** in the Vedic period, and owning a large number of cows was a sign of a **person's wealth and status.**

• It is a term used to describe a **daughter** in the Vedic period.
 
 
 
• **Gaveshna:**
 
 
• **​**It is not a term found in the Vedic texts.
 
 
 
• **Ravi:**
 
 
• **​** It is a Sanskrit word that means **'sun' **and is also the name of a Vedic deity.
 
 
 
• The Vedic period in ancient India lasted from around **1500 BCE to 500 BCE** and was characterized by the development of the **Vedic religion,** which was based on the** Vedas**, a collection of **ancient Hindu scriptures.**

questions.question: India has been ranked _________ in the Medical Tourism Index (MTI) for 2020-21 out of 46 destinations by the Medical Tourism Association.

• It is a biannual ranking of international healthcare destinations based on American perceptions.
 
• It is developed by the International Healthcare Research Center (IHRC) and is based on a survey of over 2,000 Americans.
 
• The MTI ranks countries on a scale of 1 to 100, with a higher score indicating a more attractive medical tourism destination.
 
• India has been ranked **10th** in the **Medical Tourism Index (MTI) **for **2020-21 out of 46 **destinations by the Medical Tourism Association.
 
• The following are the reasons why India is ranked 10th: 
 
 
• India offers **world-class medical facilities** and highly skilled doctors at affordable prices.
 
• The country has a **well-developed healthcare infrastructure **with advanced technology and modern equipment.
 
• India is also known for its traditional and alternative forms of medicine such as** Ayurveda, Yoga, and Naturopathy.**
 
• The government has also taken initiatives to promote **medical tourism** in the country by easing visa rules and providing incentives to medical tourists. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Informatio__**

• If India was ranked 20th, it would be a** lower ranking** and may indicate that the country needs to improve its** medical tourism facilities** and services.
 
• If India was ranked 5th, it would be a **higher ranking** and would indicate that the country is a top destination for medical tourism.

questions.question: When was the Secretary of State for India made responsible for the Government of British India by bringing about changes in the Home Government?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1858.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **1858,** the **British government **passed the **Government of India Act,** which transferred the administration of India from the** East India Company** to the British Crown.
 
• As a result, the **Secretary of State** for India was made responsible for the **Government of British India** by bringing about changes in the Home Government.
 
• This act also abolished the **East India Company** and established the **British Raj in India.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1833:**

 
 
• This was the year when the** Charter Act **was passed, which abolished the monopoly of the East India Company in the trade with India.
 
 
 
• **1857:**
 
 
• This was the year of the **Indian Rebellion of 1857,** which led to the end of the rule of the East India Company in India but did not result in significant changes in the administration of India. 
 
 
 
• **1813:**
 
 
• This was the year when the** Charter Act was passed**, which made some minor changes in the administration of India but did not transfer the responsibility of the Government of India to the Secretary of State for India.

questions.question: Which waterway provides connectivity with mainland India through the India- Bangladesh Protocol route?

• NW-2 is a waterway that connects mainland India with **Bangladesh** through the** India-Bangladesh Protocol route.**
 
• It is a 891 km long waterway that runs along the **Brahmaputra river from Sadiya in Assam to Dhubri**, and then along the river **Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly river** system from Haldia in West Bengal to Kolkata.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **NW-83 **refers to National Waterway 83, which is the **Rajpuri creek in Maharashtra.**

questions.question: The Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution of India by the __________ Amendment.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**42nd.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Fundamental Duties** were added to the Constitution of India by the **42nd Amendment** in **1976.**
 
• The amendment was brought in during the** emergency period **and was a response to the** perceived breakdown of civic sense **and **morality **in the country.
 
• The Fundamental Duties are a set of **moral obligations** that are expected of every citizen of India, and they were added to the Constitution to promote **national unity **and a** sense of responsibility **among citizens.
 
• The Fundamental Duties are **not enforceable by law,** but they serve as a reminder of the **responsibilities** that citizens have towards their country and their fellow citizens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **other options **given in the question are** not correct.**
 
• The** 73rd Amendment** was related to **Panchayati Raj,**
 
• The** 34th Amendment **was related to the land tenure and land reform acts of various states in the Ninth Schedule.
 
• The **44th Amendment **was related to the **power of the Parliament** to amend the Constitution.
 
• Hence, the **correct answer **is option 2.

questions.question: ____________ announced the bifurcation of the British Indian Empire into a secular India and Islamic Pakistan.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Louis Mountbatten.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lord Louis Mountbatten** announced the **bifurcation of the British Indian Empire **into a **secular India** and** Islamic Pakistan** on **June 3, 1947.**
 
• The plan was known as the** Mountbatten Plan **or the **3 June Plan.**
 
• The main aim of the plan was to address the demand for a **separate Muslim state** in India, which was advocated by the **All India Muslim League** led by **Muhammad Ali Jinnah.**
 
• The plan proposed the creation of** two independent dominions** of **India and Pakistan**, which would have their **own constitutions and governments,** but would remain within the **British Commonwealth.**
 
• **Lord Ripon, Lord Dalhousie, and Lord Curzon** were also British officials who served as** Viceroy of India** during the British Raj but did not announce the bifurcation of the British Indian Empire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Ripon **served as **Viceroy of India** from **1880 to 1884** and introduced various reforms, including the** Local Self-Government Act**, which provided for the establishment of** local self-government institutions** in India.
 
• **Lord Dalhousie** served as **Viceroy of India** from **1848 to 1856 **and was known for his** policy of annexation**, which led to the annexation of several **princely states** in India.
 
• **Lord Curzon** served as** Viceroy of India** from **1899 to 1905** and was known for his **administrative reforms,** including the** partition of Bengal** in **1905**, which was later revoked due to protests.
 
• Hence, the **correct answer **is option **3**, Lord Louis Mountbatten.

questions.question: Which of the following cells are found in the liver of mammals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kupffer cells.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kupffer cells** are found in the **liver of mammals.**
 
• Kupffer cells are **specialized macrophages** found in the liver, responsible for **removing foreign substances** such as bacteria and old red blood cells from the **bloodstream. ​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Purkinje cells** are a type of **neuron **found in the **cerebellum of the brain**, involved in controlling **movement and coordination.**
 
• **Microglial cells** are immune cells found in the** central nervous system,** responsible for** maintaining brain health **and responding to** injury or infection.**
 
• **Sensory cells** are specialized cells found in the **sense organs**, such as the **eyes, ears, and nose, **responsible for **detecting stimuli **and **transmitting signals **to the brain.
 
• Therefore, option 1 (Purkinje cells), option 2 (Microglial cells), and option 4 (Sensory cells) are **incorrect **as they are not found in the liver of mammals.

questions.question: The Shailendra kings who founded their empire in South-east Asia in the 8th Century AD were the followers of _____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Buddhism.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Shailendra kings** were followers of **Mahayana Buddhism.**
 
• They were known for their **patronage of Buddhist art and architecture,** including the construction of the **famous Borobudur temple **in **Java.**
 
• The Shailendra empire was based in **Java **and spread to other parts of Southeast Asia, including **Sumatra, Bali,** and parts of modern-day **Malaysia and Thailand.**
 
• The Shailendra dynasty declined in the** 9th century**, but their influence on **Southeast Asian culture** and **religion continued.**
 
• **Shaivism, Jainism, and Hinduism **were also present in Southeast Asia during this time period, but they** did not** have the same level of influence as Buddhism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shaivism** is a sect of Hinduism that worships the **god Shiva **and emphasizes **asceticism and meditation.**
 
• **Jainism** is a religion that originated in India and emphasizes **non-violence, asceticism, **and the** pursuit of spiritual liberation.**
 
• **Hinduism** is a diverse religion with many different **sects and traditions,** but it generally emphasizes the **pursuit of dharma **(righteousness),** karma** (action), and **moksha **(liberation).
 
• Hence, the **correct **answer is option 1 - Buddhism.

questions.question: Which Vitamin D analogue is used to treat hypoparathyroidism, refractory rickets and familial hypophosphatemia?

__
 
• **Ergocalciferol is **also known as **vitamin D2.**
 
• It is used to treat **hypoparathyroidism, refractory rickets, and familial hypophosphatemia** because it helps the body **absorb calcium** and **phosphorus,** which are essential for **bone health.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tacalcitol **is a** vitamin D analogue** that is primarily used to** treat psoriasis** and other **skin disorders**.

 
 
• It works by regulating the **growth and differentiation** of** skin cells.**
 
 
 
• **Tocopherol** is a form of **vitamin E,** which is important for maintaining **healthy skin and eyes**, as well as **strengthening the immune system.**
 
 
• It is **not **used to treat hypoparathyroidism, refractory rickets, or familial hypophosphatemia.
 
 
 
• **Retinol** is a form of** vitamin A,** which is important for maintaining **healthy vision, skin, and immune system.**
 
 
• It is **not** used to treat hypoparathyroidism, refractory rickets, or familial hypophosphatemia.
 
 
 
• Hence, the** correct** answer is option 3, Ergocalciferol.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of rock?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Trace rock.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Trace rock** is **not** a type of rock. 
 
• This term **does not exist** in the field of** geology.**
 
• Therefore, statement 2 is** incorrect. **
 
• The **three main types** of rocks are **igneous, metamorphic, and sedimentary. **
 
• **Igneous rocks** are formed from** cooled and solidified lava** or magma. 
 
• **Metamorphic rocks** are formed from existing rock that has been altered by **heat, pressure, or chemical reactions. **
 
• **Sedimentary rocks** are formed from the **accumulation of sediment** or organic matter.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Igneous rocks can be further classified into **intrusive** (formed inside the Earth's crust) or **extrusive (**formed on the Earth's surface) types.
 
• Metamorphic rocks can be further classified into** foliated** (having a layered or banded appearance) or** non-foliated types.**
 
• Sedimentary rocks can be further classified into **clastic **(formed from broken fragments of other rocks),** chemical** (formed from precipitation of minerals), or** organic** (formed from the remains of living organisms) types.

questions.question: From which Latin word is the s block element calcium derived?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Calx.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **s block element **Calcium is derived from the **Latin word "Calx".**
 
• Calx means** limestone or chalk**, which is a **white sedimentary rock **composed primarily of **calcium carbonate**.
 
• **Calcium** is a **chemical element **with the symbol** Ca** and atomic number **20.**
 
• It is a **reactive metal **that forms a **dark oxide-nitride layer** when exposed to air.
 
• Calcium is essential for **living organisms**, particularly in **cell physiology,** where movement of the** calcium ion** into and out of the** cytoplasm functions **as a signal for many cellular processes.

• **Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India (ICICI)** was set up in** 1955, **making it the second oldest DFI.
 
• **Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI) **was set up in** 1964,** making it the youngest DFI among the three.

• **ICICI** was converted into a** commercial bank in 1994** and is now known as ICICI Bank.
 
• **IDBI** was converted into a **commercial bank in 2019** and is now known as IDBI Bank.
 
• **Option 1**: (i) - (iii) - (ii) - This option is** incorrect** as IFCI was set up before ICICI. 
 
• **Option 3:** (ii) - (i) - (iii) - This option is **incorrect **as IDBI was set up after ICICI.
 
• **Option 4: **(i) - (ii) - (iii) - This option is **incorrect **as IDBI was set up after ICICI.

questions.question: MUDRA is a financial institution set up by the Government of India for the development and refinancing of micro unit enterprises. The full form of MUDRA is:

options.text: Micro Finance Usage Development & Refinance Agent

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Micro Units Development & Refinance Agency.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **MUDRA **stands for **Micro Units Development & Refinance Agency.**
 
• It is a **financial institution** that was set up by the **Government of India** to provide **financial assistance** to **micro unit enterprises.**
 
• The **main objective** of MUDRA is to **promote entrepreneurship **and generate **employment opportunities** in the country by providing access to credit for **small businesses.**
 
• MUDRA offers loans of up to** Rs. 10 lakhs **to micro and small enterprises under three categories -** Shishu, Kishor, and Tarun.**
 
• The loans provided by MUDRA are **collateral-free** and can be availed by both **new and existing businesses.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The other options mentioned in the question are** not the correct **full form of MUDRA.
 
• **Option 1 **(Micro Urban Development & Refinance Agency) and **Option 4** (Medium Units Development & Refinance Agency) are** incorrect** as MUDRA focuses on** micro and small enterprises** only.
 
• **Option 3** (Micro Finance Usage Development & Refinance Agent) is also** incorrect **as it does not represent the full form of MUDRA.
 
• Hence, the **correct** answer is option 2.

questions.question: The first Paralympic games were held in which year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1960.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **first Paralympic games **were held in the year** 1960.**
 
• These games were held in** Rome, Italy **and were called the **9th Annual International Stoke Mandeville Games.**
 
• The event was organized by** Sir Ludwig Guttmann,** a neurologist who worked with **World War II veterans** with **spinal cord injuries.**
 
• The games were initially meant for **wheelchair athletes** only and featured** 400 participants** from **23 countries.**
 
• The Paralympic games have since grown to become the **world's largest sports **event for **athletes with disabilities.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** 1962 is** incorrect** as the first Paralympic games were held in 1960. 
 
• **Option 3:** 1964 is** incorrect **as the third Paralympic games were held in 1964, two years after the first games.
 
• **Option 4:** 1961 is **incorrect** as the first Paralympic games were held in 1960.
